program: Wingless external raw-input to representation to prediction frontier
question: Does Wingless's already-supported fixed 256-entry four-byte raw motif mechanism learn predictive structure from independently sourced external bytes and transfer that structure across prose, code, and structured-data domains without tokenization?
hypothesis: Using the exact three-source external-exposure V1 manifest, the unchanged one-byte baseline plus fixed 256 four-byte motifs will show useful within-domain learning on each source and nonzero cross-domain transfer when trained on the other two sources. Supported requires at least 1% mean cross-domain motif coverage, positive mean cross-domain covered-position accuracy gain, positive gain on at least two of three held-out domains, and no more than 0.05 bits/byte mean degradation versus the one-byte baseline; within-domain half/half controls must show at least 3% motif coverage and 0.10 covered-position accuracy gain on every domain.

prior_evidence.interpretation: The deeper hierarchy did not justify additional structure on the fresh holdout; R1 therefore reuses the simpler flat four-byte mechanism.

external_authority.execution_requirement: A separate CKB-plane READY_CONSUME receipt bound to this exact preregistration commit and experiment identifier is required before primary execution.

raw_byte_contract.encoding: exact fetched bytes after SHA-256 verification; no decoding, Unicode normalization, tokenizer, vocabulary, subword mapping, line parsing, or inserted boundary tokens
raw_byte_contract.file_boundary_policy: reset baseline and motif window state at every source boundary

learner.baseline: same fixed 256x256 previous-byte -> next-byte uint32 counts used by WLM-LM-REAL-UTF8-BYTE-PILOT-R2; lowest-byte argmax tie break; Jeffreys smoothing
learner.motifs: same four-byte candidate construction, occurrence >=4, best-successor-count then consistency then lexicographic ranking used by R2
learner.prediction: selected exact four-byte motif successor distribution when matched, otherwise one-byte baseline

cross_domain: For each target domain, train baseline and motifs on the complete other two source files only; evaluate every next-byte position in the untouched target source.
Report motif coverage, motif-covered accuracy gain over the same training-set one-byte baseline, event reduction, and adaptive-minus-baseline bits/byte.
No target byte participates in training for its leave-one-domain-out arm.
within_domain_control: For each domain independently, split exact bytes at floor(length/2); train on first half only and evaluate second half only.
Use the identical learner, capacity, filter, smoothing, and metrics.
This control distinguishes inability to learn the domain at all from failure of cross-domain transfer.

validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identities match.

A CKB-plane READY_CONSUME receipt is bound to the exact preregistration commit, experiment identifier, manifest identity, source count, byte budget, and hosted-only execution before primary execution.
All three external source SHA-256 values and exact byte lengths match before learner construction.
Cross-domain target bytes never enter the corresponding arm's baseline counts, motif candidates, motif counts, ranking, or capacity selection.
Within-domain controls use first-half bytes only for training and second-half bytes only for evaluation.
Learner mechanics are byte-for-byte equivalent to the flat R2 one-byte baseline plus four-byte motif mechanism except for accepting verified external byte slices instead of Git blobs.
No tokenizer, parser, decoder, normalization, hierarchy, semantic labels, external model, network access inside the learner, capacity growth, or post-result tuning occurs.
Primary execution occurs only on CKB-plane-authorized hosted compute, not LINKDEADKB.
Full Go regression passes before the probe and all metrics are finite.

classification_rules.supported: All validity criteria and frozen thresholds pass, supporting cross-domain transfer of the fixed raw-byte motif representation on independent external data.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes and every within-domain control learns useful structure, but one or more frozen cross-domain transfer thresholds fail.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but the fixed motif mechanism fails the within-domain controls or shows no meaningful cross-domain predictive advantage.
classification_rules.incomplete: Authority, source retrieval, or compute interruption prevents the frozen six-arm matrix.
classification_rules.invalid: Any authority, source identity, split isolation, raw-byte identity, learner-equivalence, capacity, or qualification criterion fails.

no_post_result_tuning_rule: Do not alter sources, hashes, byte budgets, train/eval splits, motif mechanics, capacity, occurrence filter, smoothing, metrics, thresholds, controls, authority binding, or interpretation after any primary output.
